newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Kabila troops surround home of Congo opponent.
newsitem.headline: Kabila troops surround home of Congo opponent.

text.p: Soldiers from President Laurent Kabila's army surrounded the home of veteran opposition leader Etienne Tshisekedi on Thursday, hours after he addressed a student gathering, witnesses said.
"They say they have been given the order to take him away. They are armed to the teeth," Tshisekedi's adviser Marcel Mbayo told Reuters.
Kabila has banned all political parties save his Alliance and all political activity. He has refused to offer Tshisekedi a role in government.
The former Zaire prime minister's nephew, Francis Kadima, said from inside Tshisekedi's house that about 30 soldiers had entered the compound around it.

Tshisekedi said earlier at Kinshasa University that he was in touch with Kabila's Alliance to "harmonise conflicting views" on the country's institutions, but called on Kabila's Rwandan Tutsi allies to go home.
He said talks began last month, a week after Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo took power after toppling dictator Mobutu Sese Seko.
Tshiekedi was the most popular domestic opponent of Mobutu and still enjoys a strong following in Kinshasa.

Tshisekedi supporters have marched in defiance of the government ban on marches. Some marches have been broken up by soldiers firing in the air, others have been allowed to proceed -- but with the army tracking them along their route.
